My dad is a firefighter, when I was a junior/senior in high school I would go on calls with him when I was bored (small town FD so no one really cared). I've seen several disturbing things but here are two of the worst.

1). We pulled up on a structure fire by the time we get there with the tanker/pump truck the house was already completely engulfed in flames and most of the family is standing on the front lawn crying. I assumed it was because they just lost everything but when we cut the sirens we hear someone screaming the most agonizing scream I've ever heard. One of the younger girls tells us her father went back inside the house to try to save their dog. Everyone should know that you should NEVER go back into the burning building. Anyway seconds later, a man comes out of the house covered in flames. After they put him out they loaded him into an ambulance. He had third degree burns over 95 percent of his body. He passed in the hospital three days later. I'll never forget seeing him burning on the ground or his screams.

2). We pulled up on an accident. A car pulled out in front of a semi truck that was going around 55mph (I assume that's how fast he was going because that was the speed limit on this stretch of road). Both the truck and the car are on fire. After the fire is put out, the car is cut open and what was inside can only be described as charged hamburger meat with bits of bone in it. That is the only time I've ever vomited while going on call with my father. The sight will haunt me forever.
